The Transformation Edge Ltd · brand standards v1.0

The Edge brand standards

How to use the mark, the palette, the type and the words, so that everything The TransEdge Church publishes looks like it came from the same place. Every value here is read from the live design system, so this document cannot drift from the site it governs.

What the brand is for

Our vision

Our vision is to generously impact nations, building a people with God-likeness, a people who will lead and influence in all areas of life through the knowledge and wisdom of God's word.

Our mission

To discover, develop, and empower individuals to become faithful disciples of Jesus Christ. Our mission is to equip believers to influence their communities through the power of the Gospel. We are committed to building a Christian community that is youthful, creative, and purpose-driven—raising leaders who make a lasting impact in every sphere of life.

These two statements are fixed. They are reproduced exactly wherever they appear, including their punctuation. They are never rephrased, shortened or modernised, and the build fails if they are altered. The tagline is A Change is Inevitable.

The symbol

A2 Architectural Threshold. Two planes standing apart, with the way through between them. It is a one-colour mark and it holds at 16px.

The lockup

The wordmark is outlined in the supplied vector, so no typeface travels with the file and no one can rebuild it slightly wrong.

Colour

Deep Slate#303847Identity, primary button, footer
Heritage Slate#4B576EAnchor text, quiet buttons
Ember#E46F3CGraphic accent only. Never text
Ember Accessible#A94722Accent text, links, focus ring
Porcelain#F6F5F2The page ground
Ink#171D24Body text

The one rule people get wrong. Ember is the brightest colour in the palette and the most tempting, and it fails contrast as text: #E46F3C measures 2.90:1 on porcelain, below even the 3:1 needed for large text. Use #A94722 whenever ember is a word. Keep #E46F3C for rules, markers and graphics, and keep it under five per cent of any composition.

Typography

Fraunces for headings, Inter for everything else. Both open licence, so there is no fee and no per-domain licence to track.

DisplayA vision to impact nations.
Heading 1Plan your visit
Heading 2What happens on a Sunday
Heading 3Who to look for
Body 18The welcome desk is just inside the main entrance.
Body 16Tell them it is your first Sunday and someone will walk you in.
Nav 14Who We Are   New Here   Events   Give
Micro 12Supporting labels only

The 12px rule. Micro type is for supporting labels and nothing else. It is never used for instructions, access conditions, safeguarding, privacy, complaints or giving. If a person needs to read it to be safe, to get in, or to give, it is 16px.

How to use it: dos and don'ts

The symbol

Do

  • Use it in one colour, always. Deep Slate on light, porcelain reversed on dark.
  • Give it clear space of a quarter of its height on all four sides.
  • Let the gap between the planes stay exactly as drawn. The gap is the threshold.
  • Set it at 16px or larger on screen, 5mm or larger in print.

Do not

  • Never colour a plane with ember, or with anything else.
  • Never add a circle, box, outline, drop shadow or glow.
  • Never close, narrow or widen the gap to make it look tidier at small sizes.
  • Never rotate, stretch, skew or redraw it.

The lockup

Do

  • Use the supplied vector. It is already outlined, so no font travels with it.
  • Horizontal with tagline at 200px or 50mm and above.
  • Compact at 140px or 35mm, stacked at 96px or 25mm.
  • Use the reversed cut on photography and on Deep Slate.

Do not

  • Never retype the wordmark in any typeface, including Fraunces.
  • Never rebuild the lockup by placing the symbol beside live text.
  • Never set a lockup below its minimum size.
  • Never place the primary cut on a busy photograph.

Colour

Do

  • Deep Slate #303847 is the identity. It carries the mark and the primary button.
  • Porcelain #F6F5F2 is the ground. White is the raised surface.
  • Ember #E46F3C is an accent for graphics: a rule, a marker, a highlight.
  • Use the accessible cut #A94722 whenever ember is text.

Do not

  • Never let ember exceed roughly five per cent of a composition.
  • Never fill a large field or a page background with ember.
  • Never set body text in ember #E46F3C. It measures 2.90:1 and fails.
  • Never use colour as the only signal. Pair it with a word or an icon.

Typography

Do

  • Fraunces sets headings. Inter sets everything else.
  • Keep sentence case. Headings read as speech, not as signage.
  • Nav at 14px minimum. Body at 16px minimum.
  • Hold body copy between 60 and 75 characters a line.

Do not

  • Never set body, navigation, buttons, labels or legal text in Fraunces.
  • Never use 12px for instructions, access conditions, safeguarding, privacy, complaints or giving.
  • Never set a heading in all capitals, and never track a heading open.
  • Never introduce a third typeface.

Words

Do

  • Australian English.
  • Say "Penrith, Sydney" for place.
  • Write people as leaders and contributors.
  • Say what a thing is, plainly.

Do not

  • Never use an em-dash in new copy. A comma, a semicolon or a full stop.
  • Never write "a multicultural church in Jamisontown", or fix TTE to a suburb.
  • Never describe pastoral care as therapy, treatment or counselling.
  • Never imply a tax-deductible receipt for church giving.

Photography

Do

  • Photograph this congregation, as it actually is.
  • One warm grade across the whole set, shadows slightly lifted.
  • Record alt text and a consent for every published image.
  • Strip EXIF, including location, before the file leaves the camera roll.

Do not

  • Never use stock photography of people who are not part of this church.
  • Never publish an image of a child without a recorded parent or guardian consent.
  • Never arrange people to look more diverse than the room is.
  • Never crop a person at a joint, and never leave a horizon askew.

ECCS is a separate legal entity. It is DGR-endorsed, keeps its own giving, receipting, privacy notice and complaints pathway, and its services are open to anyone with no church involvement required. Never imply otherwise. Its lockup has not been drawn yet, so nothing currently renders one: an approximated mark for a separate entity is worse than none.
